Subject: Dedicated inference capacity needs + Qs on H100 vs A100 vs L4

Hi Dev,

Thanks for taking this on. Attached is a short requirements doc (acme_requirements_20260224.pdf) with our expected traffic profile for the pilot:
- 24/7 production traffic, peak concurrent sessions ~1,200 (mostly chat with 1–4 messages/session)
- Average request length: 512 tokens; 99th pct up to 2,048 tokens
- We also run batch embedding jobs overnight (1.5M texts/day)
- Soft target latency: 200ms median for chat generation, 95th < 600ms

Primary asks:
1) Which GPU SKU do you recommend for Dedicated (H100 vs A100 vs L4) given memory and perf tradeoffs?
2) Approx cost delta and suggested initial pool size for a Q2 pilot (we prefer reserved capacity but need a recommendation to pitch internally)
3) Are there reallocation/fallback suggestions if we hit load spikes?

We're looping in our solutions team (CC). Aim to finalize sizing by the end of week so we can include in procurement deck.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Holt
Head of Platform, Acme Robotics

From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Holt <sarah.holt@acme-robotics.com>

Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated inference capacity needs + Qs on H100 vs A100 vs L4

Hi Sarah — thanks for the brief and the numbers. Attaching a short set of initial sizing notes (rdw_initial_sizing_notes.pdf) to capture our assumptions. High level thoughts before we do a short call:

- Workload profile drives mixed SKU approach: large-context / high-throughput generation benefits from H100 (memory + FLOPs). Embedding-heavy and small-context low-latency chat often most cost-effective on L4. A100 sits in the middle for long-context medium-throughput workloads and is efficient for 32GB/40GB memory constrained models.

- For your expected 99th up to 2,048 tokens we need GPUs with enough memory for KV cache + model weights; H100 80GB (HBM) can host larger variants without aggressive quantization. A100 40GB will require model trimming/quantization or sharding for the largest variants. L4 (24GB) is great for lower-cost, lower-memory models and embedding fleets.

Quick question: do you plan to run the same model family across endpoints, or mix (e.g., smaller LLM for chat inference + larger generation model for long-form tasks)? Callback with 30m availability today or tomorrow to align and I'll draft a recommendation.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: dev_patel@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: INTERNAL: Quick SKU sketch for Acme (notes)

Team — internal note, copying key assumptions so Dev can present:

Assumptions taken: 1,200 concurrent sessions -> ~2.4k concurrent generation tokens on average with request tails; 1.5M embeddings/day = sustained embedding throughput. Pilot target: 50% of peak traffic (safety margin) for month 1, scale to 80–100% by month 3.

Recommendation (conservative pilot):
- H100 (80GB) x4 — reserved for: large-model long-context generators (highest memory headroom, best single-GPU perf for FP16/TF32 workloads). Keep these pinned to the largest variants to avoid OOM and to reduce inter-GPU comms.
- A100 (80GB) x8 or A100 (40GB) x12 — for mid-sized generation models and scalable throughput. A100 80GB preferred if you want fewer nodes and easier model residency; 40GB is fine with model quantization + sharding.
- L4 (24GB) x20 — for embeddings and low-latency small-context chat. L4 gives better $/embedding and is good for packing many low-memory models with high concurrency.

Cost note (very rough): H100 unit-hour ~ 3–4x L4; A100 sits ~1.5–2x L4 depending on cloud region and committed pricing. I'll attach a quick spreadsheet later with hourly burn and 3-month reserved commit estimate (h100-a100-l4_cost_model.xlsx).

Operational suggestions:
- Use routing policy: latency-first to L4 for conversation priming; fallback to A100 for mid-sized models; H100 reserved for the pinned set only.
- Autoscale burst pool (short-term spot-backed) to absorb unexpected spikes, with strict SLOs and fallback to cheaper model variants.

Will finalize numbers after we confirm which exact model families Acme wants to keep resident.

-Marissa
From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Holt <sarah.holt@acme-robotics.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: RDW - Dedicated GPU SKU recommendation for Acme pilot (attached)

Hi Sarah — great sync last week. Per our conversation and internal sizing, attached is a formal recommendation (rdw_dedicated_sku_recommendation_20260302.pdf) and the cost model (h100-a100-l4_cost_model.xlsx). Executive summary below:

Executive summary (pilot / reserved capacity month 1):
- Proposed initial pool: H100 (80GB) x6, A100 (40GB) x10, L4 (24GB) x18.
  - Rationale: this mix supports your long-context variants (H100 headroom for 2k+ token runs), gives A100 nodes to scale middle-weight generators, and provides a large L4 fleet for embeddings & low-latency chat.
- Memory vs performance tradeoffs:
  - H100 80GB: best single-GPU for large-context models, highest peak throughput for FP16/TF32, costly per-hour but minimizes cross-GPU sharding overhead. Ideal when model must run resident without partitioning.
  - A100 40/80GB: good balance; 80GB reduces need for sharding but is pricier. 40GB is common and works with quantization/sharding but adds complexity to deployment and slightly higher latency variance under load.
  - L4 24GB: lowest cost per-hour, excellent for embeddings and batched small-context work. Not suitable for very large 2k+ context models without aggressive quantization.
- Cost/Budget: Pilot reserved-commit monthly estimate (list prices adjusted for reserved discounts): ~$210k/month (H100-heavy mix). Switching H100->A100 (more A100 80GB) reduces monthly committed cost by ~25–35% depending on region and commit term. Full spreadsheet attached.
- Reliability & fallbacks: configure smart routing (latency-first for chat -> L4; capacity-first for throughput -> A100; fallback to smaller model variants on L4 if H100 capacity is exhausted). Enable autoscale for embedding jobs (spot instances acceptable) and keep a 10% surplus buffer during launch month.

Next steps:
1) Confirm which model variants you plan to run resident on H100 vs A100 vs L4 (we can help with quantization profiles).
2) Decide reserved commit term (3 vs 12 months) for pricing.
3) If you want I can provide an alternate low-cost configuration (H100 reduced to 2, more A100s + additional L4s) — I included that scenario in the attached spreadsheet.

If this looks good, we can loop in procurement to start the contract.

Best,
Dev Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Dev — thanks for the thorough recommendation and the cost scenarios. We discussed internally and want to bias more toward budget predictability for the pilot. Two asks:

1) Can you provide the alternate configuration that trims H100s to 2 and shifts capacity to A100 80GB (we prefer fewer H100s due to headcount approval limits)? What is the expected perf impact for long-form 2k token runs?
2) For embeddings: can we double L4 capacity immediately (to 36) and run the overnight embedding batch on that pool while generation uses the A100/H100 mix? Any caveats on saturating L4 for both chat concurrency and embeddings?

If you can send that short delta (numbers + expected latency degradation for 2k token p95), procurement is ready to review.

Thanks,
Sarah
From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Holt <sarah.holt@acme-robotics.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 04 Mar 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RDW - Dedicated GPU SKU recommendation for Acme pilot (attached)

Sarah — quick note in-thread so procurement has the numbers (I can also push a short addendum doc):

Alternate (budget-first) pilot mix: H100 x2, A100 80GB x14, L4 x36.
- Expected impact: For 2k token runs pinned to H100-> with H100 reduced to 2, peak concurrency for the largest variants will be constrained; we estimate p95 latency for 2k token generation will increase by ~20–35% for requests that must be sharded across A100s instead of running resident on H100. In practice: non-pinned large-model runs will see higher variance and slightly higher tail latency when H100s are saturated.
- Embedding note: doubling L4 to 36 is fine; isolate embedding jobs to a separate route and allow autoscale to reclaim spot capacity for batch jobs if needed. If you plan to run embeddings and chat from the same L4 pool during peak production hours, you'll see contention — recommend separating routing or scheduling batch runs to off-peak windows (we can enforce throughput reservation on L4 for chat).

If that aligns, I'll update the cost model and send a redlined reserved commit figure for procurement.

—Dev
